headline: Breeze deal fuels growth as controls weakness persists
summary_short: Valvoline's fiscal Q2 2026 (quarter ended March 31, 2026) revenue rose 25% y/y to $503.8M on the Breeze Autocare acquisition and 8.2% system-wide same-store-sales growth, with diluted EPS up 21% y/y to $0.35 and net income of $44.8M reversing the prior quarter's loss.
summary_long: Revenue grew 25% y/y to $503.8M on 331 net new system-wide stores (led by the $637.4M Breeze Autocare acquisition) and 8.2% same-store-sales growth from pricing and premiumization. Gross margin held roughly flat at 37.1% as store-opex growth and disposition impacts offset better product-cost leverage. Income from continuing operations rose 18% to $45.3M and diluted EPS rose 21% to $0.35, aided by profit expansion but tempered by higher SG&A and Term Loan B interest expense. The six-month effective tax rate jumped to 75.5% (from 25.8%) on nondeductible goodwill tied to the FTC-mandated divestiture of 45 acquired Breeze stores. Total debt rose to $1,657.7M after the $740M Term Loan B funded Breeze; cash was $84.7M. No guidance was issued.

drivers.explanation: Quarter was defined by the $637.4M acquisition of Breeze Autocare (204 stores) funded by a new $740M Term Loan B, with 45 acquired stores immediately divested per FTC order; revenue and profit both grew despite one-time divestiture and integration costs.

Growth of 25% y/y was primarily driven by network expansion of 331 net new system-wide stores (Breeze acquisition and other openings) plus 8.2% same-store-sales growth from higher average ticket, pricing, premiumization and transaction trends, partly offset by disposition activity.

Dollar growth of 24.3% y/y reflected contributions from acquired stores and favorable service mix, partly offset by higher network-expansion costs including depreciation and higher labor/service-delivery costs; margin was roughly flat at 37.1% vs 37.3%.

Income from continuing operations grew 18% to $45.3M, driven by profit expansion from operations, partially offset by higher SG&A investment (outside services, talent, advertising) and higher interest expense tied to the new Term Loan B.
Adjusted EBITDA rose 28% y/y on gross-profit expansion, higher volumes, network-growth contributions, and pricing/cost-efficiency gains, more than offsetting dispositions and higher SG&A spend.

Six-month effective tax rate jumped to 75.5% from 25.8% because nondeductible goodwill on the FTC-required Breeze divestiture drove a $20.0M unfavorable tax effect plus $6.3M tax on the taxable gain; the quarterly rate was 23.9% vs 24.8% a year earlier.
Diluted EPS rose to $0.35 from $0.29 a year earlier, tracking the 18% growth in income from continuing operations on a roughly flat diluted share count.
